findings.title: An appointment can wait without disappearing

findings.mechanism: The focus carriers صَفًّا and مَّوْعِدًا meet the appointed-time and mercy carriers in 18:58 and the settlement, destruction, and repeated appointment in 18:59; the contact turns an isolated denial into a pericope-wide relation between delay, presentation, and consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive patience and certainty together: a delayed consequence is not thereby cancelled, and the same appointment reaches both the presented persons and ruined communities.
findings.containment: This is a pericope-bound contextual resonance, not a claim that every occurrence of mercy, settlement, or destruction has the same lexical sense, nor a claim that delay is the only purpose of the appointment.

epistemic.reason: The channel source is trusted and all cited carriers are supplied, but the cross-ayah synthesis remains a contextual macro relation rather than a direct lexical assertion.

findings.title: The interval is mercy, not absence
findings.claim: The focus's appointment can be read as a divinely made deadline whose interval is merciful rather than empty: punishment is not hastened, but the endpoint remains fixed and offers no refuge when reached.
findings.mechanism: The focus appointment and making occurrences meet 18:58 mercy, denied acceleration, repeated appointment, and denied refuge, then meet 18:59 destruction and another appointed time; the later contrast turns delay into a bounded interval and scales the mechanism to the towns.
findings.reader_payoff: The apparent silence between claim and consequence becomes legible as an interval with its own function, while the eventual boundary remains concrete and inescapable.
findings.containment: This is a legacy-unbound attributed reading and remains distinct from the broader channel account of appointment across the pericope. Mercy may explain postponed punishment while the focus appointment remains a broader term.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace has complete exact anchors and the focus return, but the interpretation of delay as a merciful interval is attributed contextual evidence.
